# Changelog: Agentic SDLC Workflow

## Requirements and design

- Captured the approved blog requirements: account registration/login, persistent inactivity-limited sessions, a public chronological feed with search and four sort modes, and author-only post creation/edit/deletion.
- Documented non-functional security expectations and excluded image uploads, password reset/OTP, and rich-text editing.
- Designed a same-origin modular application with server-side authorization and persistence.
- Reviewed the architecture against the requirements and recorded follow-up decisions for feed chronology, timestamp labels, navigation, delete confirmation, password policy, and bounded inputs.
- Produced a prioritized implementation plan with foundation, persistence, authentication, feed, authoring, and verification tasks.

## Implementation

- Added the Node.js application and npm scripts/dependencies, SQLite schema/access, server routes, validation, session behavior, and static client assets.
- Added the browser flows for registration, login, feed browsing, search/sort, post reading, and authoring.
- Updated the README with setup, run, behavior, security, and deployment guidance.
- Added `.gitignore` rules to keep generated `node_modules/` and local `data/` database files out of commits.

## Review and corrections

- Code review identified two P2 correctness findings:
  1. HTML password length limits counted UTF-16 code units while server policy counted Unicode code points.
  2. The JSON request-body cap could reject valid 10,000-code-point post content, and the oversized request error was reported as HTTP 500.
- Fixed the password input policy in `public/app.js` to count code points and align its accepted limits with server validation.
- Raised the JSON parser cap in `server.js` to support the documented maximum content and mapped oversized requests to HTTP 413.
- Added `test/server.test.js` with one focused integration regression test covering too-short and valid Unicode passwords, maximum-size CJK post content, and an oversized request response.
- Recorded the review findings and follow-up verification in `artifacts/code-review.md` and `artifacts/verification.md`.

## Verification and delivery

- `npm.cmd run check` passed, checking syntax in `server.js`, `db.js`, and `public/app.js`.
- `npm.cmd test` passed: 1 focused integration test, 0 failures.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser acceptance, broad end-to-end acceptance coverage, production deployment behavior, and realistic-volume performance remain unverified and are not claimed.
- Prepared the PR description and reviewer checklist. Generated dependency and runtime data directories remain excluded.
